title: Meeting Guitar Slim and building the band with Eddie Langlois
summary: Slim came to him with a trio; Stovall combined it with his band, added Eddie Langlois, and the guitarists' walking-the-bar act made the band in demand.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Now I can start to tell you about Slim, because this is time for him to come in right now. So later I met, later I met Gitar Slim.
Wait, who was your first big, your hottest act, your first hot act that you were in? Well, well, somebody trying to get some? Yeah. S-U-P? I'm going. I got it.
Well, actually, let me go in, let me start from Slim on, then I'll bring you in.
Okay, okay, when did you meet Slim? What was it?

I don't remember the year, I don't remember the year now of Hans, I don't remember him, but anyway, Slim came to me. I was living downtown on Utrip Street, and he had three pieces with him. Well, see, I had this band already with about six, seven pieces. So, I told him, I said, well, man, I said, I've got a good band. He said, man, I can improve your business, you know. I said, come over and hear me. I said, I went over, he's working over the river over here then, or the place over there, I can't think of the name of the place. So, he had three pieces with him, a drum, guitar, no, drum, piano, and the saxophone guitar.
Do you know who the band was?

Well, he called it his band, I don't remember the name. You don't remember the band? Yeah, I don't remember the band. I don't remember who was in the band, yes. He had a boy named Harry Smith, which is a minister now.

And then he had another boy named Oscar Moore, used to be like at the Dewdrop for years. I don't remember Oscar, he's a drummer. So what we did, we laid two pieces out, we laid one piece out of the band off, we just laid one piece out of the drummer, so he had a bit of drum in the head. And we just kept the piano player, we made the band a little bigger. So we got to traveling, and we had another little boy with us from here, his name was Eddie Langlois, we called him Billy Eddie, his name was Eddie Langlois. So he was in the band, and him and Slim would work together. They had fifty feet of water on the guitar. Each one had that. So they would walk on top of the bar, walk all on tables, you know. And man, Ben has just got to come in like you're pouring water in a pitcher, you know. Everybody wanted to book that band, you know. You see that little boy on the main walking the tables, walking the bars, and they'd go all outside with the guitar, you wouldn't see them, just hear the music on the stage, you know where he is, he's got a long run, you know. So to make the story start, we just really built up, we got up to, you know, we was in top bracket. So a guy heard us in Monroe, Louisiana, from Nashville, and he went back and told the guy who owned the club in Nashville about this band he heard. We didn't have no records working out, you know. And we played a ballad of blues with Best Domino in Monroe, that's how it was. So this kid called me out of Nashville, and we made a deal. He said, his name was Grady, I don't remember the first name, but he owned Grady's Club on the fourth floor of a building there. He heard something like, Grady. So he called me and told me he would send me transportation, come up to an audition, you know. So I accepted transportation, because what I was going to do, I was going to book myself on the way up there anyway, you see.
